newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan c/a surplus rises 15.4 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: Japan c/a surplus rises 15.4 pct in February.

text.p: The surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose 15.4 percent to 865.2 billion yen in February from a year earlier, the Ministry of Finance announced on Monday.
The surplus in merchandise trade alone also rose 2.9 percent to 878.0 billion yen from the same month a year earlier.
At Monday's rate of around 125 yen to the dollar, the current account surplus in February amounted to $6.92 billion, while the merchandise trade surplus was $7.02 billion.
The rise in the current account surplus was largely in line with forecasts by economists, who had expected an increase due to the weakness of the yen.
In a Reuters poll, the average of economists' forecasts had been for a current account surplus of 801.1 billion yen ($6.40 billion).
The Finance Ministry announced last month that Japan's trade surplus rose 6.5 percent in February from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen ($5.49 billion), the first increase since November 1994.
